glossary.Crohn's disease: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gut, with patchy, full-thickness inflammation.
glossary.ulcerative colitis: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease of the colon only, with continuous inflammation starting at the rectum.
glossary.rectal bleeding: Blood passed from the back passage.
glossary.urgency: A sudden, hard-to-delay need to open the bowels.
glossary.ileocaecal valve: The valve where the small bowel (ileum) joins the large bowel (caecum).
glossary.RIF: Right iliac fossa: the lower right part of the abdomen.
glossary.skin tags: Small soft flaps of skin, here around the anus.
glossary.fissures: Small tears in the lining of the anal canal.
glossary.colonoscopy: A camera passed through the anus to look at the whole colon and take biopsies.
glossary.anal verge: The outer edge of the anal canal, where it meets the skin.
glossary.transverse colon: The part of the colon running across the upper abdomen.
glossary.proctosigmoiditis: Inflammation of the rectum and sigmoid colon.
glossary.exacerbation: A flare-up when the disease suddenly gets worse.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin: the oxygen-carrying protein in red cells, measured to detect anaemia.
glossary.ESR: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: a non-specific blood marker of inflammation.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein: a blood marker that rises quickly with inflammation or infection.
glossary.systemic toxicity: Signs of whole-body illness such as fever, fast pulse and low blood pressure.
glossary.neutrophilic leucocytosis: A raised white cell count driven by neutrophils.
glossary.CA 19-9: A tumour marker in the blood that is raised in cholangiocarcinoma and pancreatic cancer.
glossary.ALT: Alanine aminotransferase: a liver enzyme that rises mainly with liver cell damage.
glossary.extra-intestinal manifestations: Features of a gut disease that affect other parts of the body, such as the eyes, skin and joints.
glossary.ankylosing spondylitis: Chronic inflammatory arthritis of the spine and sacroiliac joints that causes back stiffness.
glossary.uveitis: Inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, causing a red, painful eye.
glossary.scleritis: Painful inflammation of the white of the eye that can threaten sight.
glossary.renal stones: Kidney stones; more common in Crohn's because of altered fat and oxalate absorption.
glossary.anal fissure: A small tear in the anal lining causing pain on opening the bowels.
glossary.seronegative: An arthritis with negative rheumatoid factor in the blood.
glossary.vitamin B12 deficiency: Lack of vitamin B12, absorbed in the terminal ileum, causing anaemia and nerve damage.
glossary.biopsy: A small piece of tissue taken for examination under the microscope.
glossary.perforation: A hole through the bowel wall.
glossary.mucin depletion: Loss of the mucus normally produced by the bowel lining.
glossary.vascular markings: Blood vessels normally visible through the bowel lining at endoscopy.
glossary.submucosal fibrosis: Scarring in the layer under the bowel lining.
glossary.serosal: Relating to the outer surface layer of the bowel.
glossary.MRI small bowel: MRI scan of the small intestine used to map the extent of Crohn's disease.
glossary.perianal abscess: A collection of pus next to the anus.
glossary.neutropenia: A low neutrophil count, raising the risk of serious infection.
glossary.TB: Tuberculosis: infection that can reactivate when TNF is blocked.
glossary.biologics: Drugs made from antibodies or proteins that block specific immune molecules, such as infliximab.
glossary.immunosuppressants: Drugs that damp down the immune system.
glossary.induction: The first phase of treatment, aiming to bring a flare under control.
glossary.maintenance: Ongoing treatment to keep the disease in remission.
glossary.prednisolone: An oral corticosteroid used to bring IBD flares under control.
glossary.corticosteroid: A steroid drug that reduces inflammation, such as prednisolone or hydrocortisone.
glossary.tacrolimus: A calcineurin inhibitor immunosuppressant used as rescue therapy in UC.
glossary.panproctocolectomy: Surgical removal of the whole colon and rectum.
glossary.prophylactic: Given to prevent a problem rather than treat one.
glossary.VTE: Venous thromboembolism: a clot in a deep vein or the lungs; IBD flares raise this risk.
glossary.NG tube: Nasogastric tube: passed through the nose into the stomach to decompress it or feed.
glossary.ciprofloxacin: A quinolone antibiotic used with metronidazole for perianal Crohn's.
glossary.incision and drainage: Cutting open an abscess to let the pus out.
glossary.allopurinol: A gout drug that blocks breakdown of azathioprine, so together they can cause dangerous bone marrow suppression.
glossary.stricture: A narrowing of the bowel, often from scarring.
glossary.cytokine: A signalling protein that immune cells use to talk to each other.
glossary.granuloma: A small cluster of immune cells that forms around something the body cannot clear.
